harbor_antrieb_executor.summary:
On node1 (RHEL 7.9), installed rootless podman 1.6.4 (via CentOS-7 vault extras/base/updates repos, since RHEL entitlement wasn't available), created the unprivileged appsvc user with a subuid/subgid range, enabled lingering for appsvc, and deployed a containerized nginx web app (docker.io/library/nginx:alpine) as appsvc, port-mapped to 8080. The container is managed by a systemd --user unit (container-webapp.service) enabled under appsvc's user manager, and the user manager itself is enabled to start at system boot (user@1001.service enabled against default.target/multi-user.target) so it runs without appsvc ever having an active login session. Verified this survives an actual node reboot: boot ID changed, appsvc has zero login sessions, user@1001.service and the container-webapp.service came up automatically, and the app returns HTTP 200 on $NODE_IP:8080.

Non-obvious fixes required along the way: restored a missing user@.service systemd template unit (stripped from this image's systemd package), enabled user.max_user_namespaces sysctl, fixed newuidmap/newgidmap capability conflicts, installed missing fuse/fuse3 packages for fuse-overlayfs, worked around a podman rootless bug where the reexec'd child fatally aborts if it can't chdir back to the invoking shell's original (inaccessible) cwd, disabled default seccomp (kernel 3.10 syscall-table mismatch caused nginx's pwrite to fail with EPERM), and replaced the buggy auto-generated Type=forking/PIDFile unit with a reliable Type=simple unit. Discovered that this systemd 219 build's logind does not reliably auto-start lingering users' sessions at boot, so the user@1001.service was additionally enabled directly as a system unit for reliability.
actions_performed: Enabled CentOS-7 vault extras/base/updates yum repos (no RHEL subscription available) and installed podman 1.6.4 plus dependencies
Created appsvc user with home dir; deduplicated/normalized /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid entries (appsvc:165536:65536)
Ran `loginctl enable-linger appsvc`
Restored missing /usr/lib/systemd/system/user@.service template unit and daemon-reloaded
Set user.max_user_namespaces=28633 via sysctl (persisted in /etc/sysctl.d/99-userns.conf)
Installed fuse and fuse3 packages (fusermount3 was missing, breaking fuse-overlayfs)
Diagnosed and fixed newuidmap/newgidmap: removed conflicting setuid+filecaps combination that caused rootless uid/gid mapping failures
Configured appsvc rootless podman storage (~/.config/containers/storage.conf) using overlay driver with fuse-overlayfs mount_program and ignore_chown_errors
Diagnosed and worked around a podman rootless reexec bug that fatally aborts on inherited-cwd chdir failure (ran podman from /tmp instead of the harness's default cwd)

Pulled docker.io/library/nginx:alpine and diagnosed an nginx pwrite(/run/nginx.pid) EPERM caused by podman's default seccomp profile mismatching the RHEL7 3.10 kernel; fixed with --security-opt seccomp=unconfined
Created container 'webapp' as appsvc with -p 8080:80 and seccomp=unconfined
Generated and then hand-corrected a systemd --user unit (container-webapp.service) as Type=simple running `podman start -a webapp`, replacing the flaky Type=forking/PIDFile generated unit
Enabled container-webapp.service under appsvc's systemd --user instance
Enabled user@1001.service directly at the system level (multi-user.target) for reliable boot-time start, since logind's linger-triggered auto-start was found unreliable on this systemd 219 build
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot id, service states, zero login sessions, HTTP 200)

Performed the mandatory single-node restart via `systemctl reboot`, polled until reachable again, and verified changed boot id, recovered user session manager, recovered container service, and working HTTP endpoint with no login session for appsvc
Re-enabled SELinux enforcing mode (was briefly set permissive for diagnostics) and re-verified functionality

evidence.requirement: Containerized web app runs as unprivileged appsvc user, serving on port 8080
evidence.summary: Image pulled and run as appsvc via rootless podman with -p 8080:80; curl to $NODE_IP:8080 returns HTTP 200

evidence.requirement: Container starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
evidence.summary: Captured baseline (boot id f0f8b8e0), issued systemd reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot id (ddf54967) after fixing enablement, and confirmed appsvc has zero loginctl sessions while user@1001.service and container-webapp.service are active and nginx serves HTTP 200

evidence.requirement: Lingering configured for appsvc so its systemd user session persists without login
evidence.summary: loginctl enable-linger appsvc set State=lingering/Linger=yes; confirmed Linger=yes persisted and Sessions=empty after reboot

evidence.requirement: Boot identity changed as direct proof of restart (not just elapsed time/service restart)
evidence.summary: /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id compared before (f0f8b8e0-5ebe-465b-8853-020a1ffc5b08) and after (ddf54967-b958-4c66-b543-2943121c9dc5) the systemctl reboot, with uptime -s showing a fresh boot timestamp

evidence.requirement: Reliability gap identified and fixed: logind linger-only auto-start was insufficient on this systemd 219 build
evidence.summary: First reboot attempt (with only enable-linger) showed user@1001.service inactive and container in 'Created' (not running) state; fixed by additionally enabling user@1001.service as a system unit, verified by the second reboot succeeding
